articleTitle: A TID and SEE Characterization of Multi-Terabit COTS 3D NAND Flash
abstract: Single-event effects and total ionizing dose testing are described for a 32-layer NAND flash memory, in both SLC and MLC configurations, with special considerations for unique three-dimensional test results. Extraction of three-dimensional heavyion test data presents a unique visualization of angular effects in NAND flash. Pattern dependence differences between SLC and MLC mode are noted, along with slightly non-uniform angular cross-section results due to the complex volume. Finally, TID data under different operating and bias conditions shows that the failure point remains the higher-voltage erasure circuitry.

articleTitle: Total Dose and Heavy Ion Radiation Response of 55 nm Avalanche Technology Spin Transfer Torque MRAM
abstract: The total dose and heavy ion radiation responses of 55 nm non-volatile spin transfer torque memory devices from Avalanche Technology are presented, and show these devices to be inherently largely radiation tolerant.

articleTitle: The Aerospace Corporation’s Compendium of Recent Single Event Effect Results
abstract: Single Event Effect testing using heavy ions and protons was performed on several commercial components to determine the response of these components to the space radiation environment.

articleTitle: Recent SEE Results for Snapdragon Processors
abstract: SEE test results are presented for the Snapdragon 801, 835 and 845 processors. The focus is on the performance of the processors under a normal work environment. Testing was performed to get an understanding of the crash and bit error performance. In the case of the 801, SEL data were also collected.

articleTitle: Degradation Measurement of Kinect Sensor Under Fast Neutron Beamline
abstract: The neutron-induced degradation of depth images acquired using a Kinect sensor is investigated through the standard metrics. The evaluated metrics indicate saturation of degradation after several hours of exposure, which is recovered through annealing.

articleTitle: Single-Event Characterization of the 16 nm FinFET Xilinx UltraScale+TM RFSoC Field-Programmable Gate Array under Proton Irradiation
abstract: This study examines the single-event upset and single-event latch-up susceptibility of the Xilinx 16nm FinFET Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoC FPGA in proton irradiation. Results for SEU in configuration memory, BlockRAM memory, and device SEL are given.

articleTitle: Single Event Effects Testing for the ADC12DJ3200QML-SP 12-bit, Dual 3.2-GSPS Single 6.4-GSPS, RF-Sampling, JESD204B, Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC)
abstract: The effects of heavy-ion irradiation on the single-event effect performance of the Texas Instruments ADC12DJ3200QML-SP and its JESD204B serialized interface were characterized using the K500 Cyclotron facility at Texas A&M University. The results demonstrate latch-up immunity up to LET<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">EFF</inf> = 120 MeV-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg at T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">J</inf> = 125°C while operating at the maximum recommended operating supply voltages. Dynamic cross sections for the code error rate of the device and the serialized interface are also presented.

articleTitle: Radiation Effects Testing of Selected Voltage Regulator Microcircuits with Heavy Ions and Protons
abstract: We present observations of heavy ion and proton induced radiation effects on selected commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) voltage regulator integrated microcircuits.

articleTitle: Compendium of Recent Radiation Test Results from the Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory
abstract: Total Ionizing Dose (TID), Enhanced Low Dose Rate Sensitivity (ELDRS), and Single Event Effect (SEE) test results are presented for a variety of analog, digital, mixed signal, and Radio Frequency (RF) devices.

articleTitle: Radiation Effects Characterization of Commercial Multi-Channel Digital to Analog Converters for Spaceflight Applications
abstract: This paper presents recent heavy ion single-event effects test results for commercial off the shelf multi-channel digital to analog converter devices. Data was taken in CY18 for device evaluation for use in a NASA space observatory mission.

articleTitle: Single-Event Characterization of a Stratix® 10 FPGA Using Neutron Irradiation
abstract: FPGAs are being used in data center applications in large quantities. Single-event upsets (SEUs) occur more frequently within large-scale deployments of SRAM-based FPGAs. This work estimates the neutron cross section for SEUs in the configuration memory and memory blocks of a 14-nm FinFET Stratix 10 FPGA. SEU data was collected using a custom SEU data collection system. The developed system takes advantage of SEU mitigation features available on the device. The New York City FIT rate for SEUs is estimated to be 3.2 FIT per Mbit for configuration memory and 7.1 FIT per Mbit for memory blocks.

articleTitle: Room Temperature Radiation Testing of a 500 °C Durable 4H-SiC JFET Integrated Circuit Technology
abstract: Total ionizing dose (TID) and single-event effect (SEE) room-temperature radiation test results are presented for developmental prototype 4H-SiC junction field effect transistor (JFET) semiconductor integrated circuits (ICs) that have demonstrated prolonged operation in extremely high-temperature (500 °C) environments. The devices tested demonstrated over 7 Mrad(Si) TID tolerance and no destructive SEE susceptibility.

articleTitle: Heavy Ion Single Event Latchup Measurements of a Focal Plane Imager at Room and Cryogenic Temperatures
abstract: Heavy ion-induced Single Event Latchup (SEL) is characterized in a CMOS focal plane array Readout Integrated Circuit (ROIC) at room temperature and 225 K. The LET threshold at room temperature is between 22 and 24 MeV-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg. The part is SEL immune at 225 K.

articleTitle: Radiation-Induced Errors at Elevated Linear Energy Transfer Levels and Magnetic Error Rate Interactions in Magnetic Tunnel Junctions
abstract: The response to heavy ion irradiation of Magnetic Tunnel Junctions (MTJs), in 16Mb toggle-bit Magneto-Resistive Random Access Memories (Toggle-MRAMs) at the 150 nm node that are QML V and Q qualified, and in 256Mb STT-MRAMs for sub-100 nm nodes, has been reported in previous work for normal LET (Linear Energy Transfer) levels up to approximately 88 MeV-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg. In this work, heavy-ion results are reported, which are understood to be novel and to be the first tests of their kind, which were performed on 16Mb Toggle-MRAMs at effective LET levels up to approximately 145 MeV-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg, using oblique-angle heavy-ion irradiation. Hard errors in MTJ bits were observed in this elevated effective LET testing. Initial magnetic bit error counts are also reported for 16Mb Toggle-MRAMs across temperature, ranging from -55 °C to +125 °C. These findings, combined with MTJ endurance that is greater to much greater than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> write and read cycles, support low error rate operation with low magnetic error rates even at elevated effective LET levels.

articleTitle: Total Dose Performance at High and Low Dose Rate of CMOS, biCMOS, and Bipolar Low Dropout Voltage Regulators
abstract: Results of Cobalt-60 irradiation of low dropout voltage regulators at high and low dose rates are presented. Performance in the space radiation environment is discussed.

articleTitle: Radiation Evaluation of the Texas Instruments TPS7H2201-SP eFuse
abstract: Single Event Effects and Total Ionizing Dose characterization results for the TPS7H2201-SP are summarized. The data shows the device is SEL-free (at T$\approx$125 °C), SEB-free, SEGR-free, SEFI-free and SET-free (at T$\approx$23 °C) up to LET<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">EFF</inf>=75 MeV$\cdot$ cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg and across the full electrical specifications. The eFuse is also ELDRS-free with a TID rating of 100 krad(Si).

articleTitle: Characterization of the Effects of Proton-Induced Total Ionizing Dose and Displacement Damage on the UC1875 Controller
abstract: This paper explores the combined effects of total ionizing dose and displacement damage caused by 250 MeV protons on the Texas Instruments UC1875 controller. Two fluences – 4×1011 and 1×1012 protons/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> – were used for this test.

articleTitle: Proton Characterization of RTG4 Flash-Based FPGA for LEO Environment
abstract: The single-event response of the RTG4 flash-based FPGA is characterized using 64 and 200 MeV proton sources. Several blocks are tested, including self-corrected triple module redundant (STMR) flip-flops with SET filter enabled and disabled, micro SRAM ($\mu$ SRAM), large SRAM (LSRAM), phase locked loop (PLL), serializer/deserializer (SERDES) and fabric double data rate controller (FDDRC). In-beam power on reset (POR) and reprogramming/verify are evaluated for the first time in proton environment.

articleTitle: Fast-neutron testing at the University of Washington Medical Cyclotron Facility
abstract: Because of the cascade of secondary particles, including neutrons, produced in the shielding of large spacecraft, it is important to test the reliability of electronic devices exposed to energetic (fast) neutrons. Additionally, devices located near accelerators, such as those found in cancer therapy clinics, can be exposed to a substantial fluence of neutrons.The energy spectrum of the primary neutron beam has been modeled and benchmarked extensively. To cater to a broader community interested in fast-neutron testing, we have been developing a series of neutron spectra based on scattering the primary neutron beam. A stack of plastic used to scatter the beam, was simulated using MCNP6.2 to analyze the spectra at various locations. We also use MCNP6.2 to investigate the potential of developing a softer neutron spectrum using graphite to reduce the low energy absorption which occurs in the plastic.

articleTitle: TID and SEE Responses of Rad-Hard A/D Converter RHFAD128
abstract: This paper reports on the different responses observed during heavy ion irradiation and Total Ionizing dose test on a newly developed Rad-Hard, 8-Channel, 50ksps to 1Msps, 12-Bit A/D Converter, called RHFAD128.

articleTitle: Single Event Dielectric Rupture Characterization of Microchip High Voltage Devices
abstract: Experimental results on single-event hard errors (SEDR-SEGR) of high voltages MOS transistors, and capacitors are presented. A Pre-and post-radiation characterization has been carried out and safe operating areas have been established.

articleTitle: Radiation Evaluation of the ADS1278-SP Radiation Hardened 24-Bit 8-Ch Simultaneous-Sampling ADC
abstract: ADS1278-SP is a Radiation Hardened 24-Bit 8-Ch Simultaneous-Sampling Delta-Sigma ADC for Space applications. ADS1278-SP has been characterized to pass Total dose level of up to 50 krad(Si). Single Event Heavy Ion testing showed that ADS1278-SP was SEL-free up to LETeff =75 MeV-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/</sup>/mg, and has very low cross section for SET.

articleTitle: Heavy Ion Test Results for the MOOG Broad Reach BRE440 Processor
abstract: SEE test results are presented for the CPU, cache, DRAM interface unit, and associated processorlocal bus circuitry of the radiation-hardened BRE440, a PowerPC 440-based SOC processor fabricated on the Honeywell HX5000 150 nm technology node.

articleTitle: Single Event Effect Test Results for Candidate Spacecraft Electronics
abstract: We present test results on the immunity of a variety of candidate spacecraft ICs and modules to proton and heavy ion induced single event effects. Tested devices include analog devices, such as comparators, amplifiers, regulators, optocouplers, DC/DC converters, and transistors.

articleTitle: 0.040 rad(Si)/s total dose testing of Renesas parts proposed for the Europa Clipper mission
abstract: We report the results of collaborative total ionizing dose (TID) radiation testing carried out by Renesas Electronics America (‘Renesas’) and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (‘JPL’) in support of the Europa Clipper program. The program investigated the TID response of seven Renesas part types as listed in Table 1. The low dose rate of 0.040 rad(Si)/s and the total dose of 300 krad(Si) are specific to the Europa Clipper radiation requirements.

articleTitle: Radiation Degradation of Temperature Dependences of Electrical Parameters of Bipolar Operational Amplifiers
abstract: The impact of radiation degradation on the temperature dependence of electrical parameters of bipolar operational amplifiers is presented. Results of the researches can improve our understanding of physical and circuit radiation effects in bipolar operational amplifiers.

articleTitle: A comparison of 0.040 rad(Si)/s and 0.010 rad(Si)s total dose results of Renesas parts proposed for the Europa Clipper mission
abstract: We compare the results of 0.040 rad(Si)/s total ionizing dose (TID) radiation testing with existing 0.010 rad(Si)/s data taken from routine characterization and acceptance testing. The testing was carried out by Renesas Electronics America (`Renesas’) and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL’) in support of the Europa Clipper program. The program investigated the TID response of seven Renesas part types as listed in Table 1. The 0.040 rad(Si)/s dose rate is specific to the Europa Clipper program.

articleTitle: Single Event Upset Characterization of the Cyclone V Field Programmable Gate Array Using Proton Irradiation
abstract: Proton induced SEU cross-sections of certain functional blocks of the Cyclone V FPGA are presented. Upset rates in the space radiation environment are estimated.

articleTitle: Single-event Evaluation of Xilinx 16nm UltraScale+™ High-Bandwidth Memory Enabled FPGA
abstract: Single-event characterization of a Xilinx 16nm UltraScale+ Virtex high bandwidth memory (HBM)-enabled FPGA was performed using both the 64 MeV proton beam at Crocker Nuclear Laboratory and the neutron beam at LANSCE. Both single-event upset (SEU) and single-event functional interrupt (SEFI) analysis were performed on HBM stacks, fabric interface and HBM interface.

articleTitle: Single Event Transient and Single Event Upset Characterization of a Cobham Designed 3.125 Gbps Crosspoint Switch
abstract: Single event transient and single event upset characterization data will be presented for the newly designed and fabricated Cobham radiation-hardened UT65CML8X8FD 3.125 Gbps Crosspoint Switch (XPS).

articleTitle: A SET Study on SRAM Memory
abstract: We report a MBU-like transient test result on 4Mb SRAM die during HI SEE test. Further SEE laser test study showed that the root cause is the floating pads to conFigure & probe the die creating transient SEFI. A mitigation was also proposed and verified in the following laser and HI tests..

articleTitle: Single Event Effect Characterization of High Density SRAMs in Bulk and SOI Technologies
abstract: The single event effects of 32M Bulk epitaxial CMOS SRAM and 16M SOI CMOS SRAM are characterized with heavy ion. The upset rates of SRAMs in GEO orbit are calculated using SEU cross section characteristics. Both of the two radiation-hardened SRAMs exhibit expected SEE resistance. The devices are single event latchup immune and the estimated upset rates are less than 1x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup> errors/bit•day. The penetration depth of heavy ion and upset pattern of the SEU test are analyzed.

articleTitle: Proton, Gamma, and Neutron Irradiation of a 10V Precision Voltage Reference
abstract: Electrical performance data was collected on a 10V voltage reference exposed to proton, γ-ray, and γ- ray + neutron irradiation. Comparisons are made between the results from the different irradiation methods and proton-induced SET results are reported.

articleTitle: Heavy Ion SEE Testing of Microchip Integrated Motor Controller LX7720
abstract: The Heavy Ion SEE testing results of the Microchip radiation hardened analog mixed-signal motor controller IC, the LX7720, are presented, including the complete SEL data and SET/SEU for the different functions.

articleTitle: Laser-Induced Micro SEL Characterization of SRAM Devices
abstract: This paper presents micro single event latch-up characterization of SRAM by laser backside testing. The SEL threshold and the detailed micro SEL features have been investigated by laser automatic scanning experiment. The micro SEL results can give the reference for the hardness assurance in circuit system level.

articleTitle: Test Results of Proton Single-Event Effects Conducted by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory
abstract: This paper reports recent single-event effects results for a variety of microelectronic devices that include SRAM, FPGA, Flash Memory and a Linear Voltage Regulator. The data was collected to evaluate these devices for possible use in NASA missions.

articleTitle: SEE Testing of DDR2 Memories
abstract: Single event effect (SEE) testing was performed on three DDR2 devices that varied in density and feature sizes. Testing was performed up to LET = 57 MeV-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg. The parts were characterized for a variety of SEE, including multi-bit upsets (MBU) and single event functional interrupts (SEFI).

articleTitle: Characterization of the Effects of 250 MeV Proton-Induced Total Ionizing Dose and Displacement Damage on the HCPL-625K Optocoupler
abstract: This paper explores the combined effects of total ionizing dose and displacement damage caused by 250 MeV protons on the Broadcom HCPL-625K optocoupler. Proton fluences up to 4x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup> were used for this radiation test.

articleTitle: Radiation Effects Characterization of TI THS4541-SP Rail-to-Rail Output 850 Mhz Fully Differential Amplifier
abstract: THS4541-SP is a Rail-to-Rail Output 850Mhz Fully Differential Amplifier being released for Space applications. THS4541-SP has been characterized to pass Total Dose (TID) of 100 krad(Si) under both high and low dose rates. It is shown to be Latch-up immune upto 93.98 MeV-cm2/mg.

articleTitle: Heavy ion Single Event Effects (SEE) results for PWM5032 Pulse Width Modulator Controller
abstract: H eavy Ion (HI) testing of the PWM5032 PWM Controller was performed at Texas A&M University (TAMU). Testing resulted in no destructive failures (either SEL or SEGR). Non-destructive events, such as transients and frequency variations were observed and characterized with candidate Weibull fitting parameters as determined herein.

articleTitle: Total Dose Homogeneity of Commercial off the Shelf biCMOS and Bipolar Voltage References at Low Dose Rate
abstract: Total dose homogeneity of biCMOS and bipolar voltage references at low dose rate is presented. Radiation hardness assurance implications and performance in the space radiation environment are discussed.

articleTitle: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center’s Compendium of Total Ionizing Dose, Displacement Damage Dose, and Single-Event Effects Test Results
abstract: Total ionizing dose, displacement damage dose, and single-event effect testing were performed to characterize and determine the suitability of candidate electronics for NASA space utilization. Devices tested include optoelectronics, digital, analog, bipolar devices, and FPGAs.

articleTitle: Radiation Test Results for Glenair 5 Gbps and 40 Gbps (4x10 Gbps) Optical Transceivers
abstract: We evaluated the effects of heavy ions, protons, neutrons and gamma (Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>) on high speed commercial optical transceivers for potential use in space systems. Test results from heavy ion and proton testing of the Glenair 050-301, also known as “Size 8”, 5 Gbps opto- electronic transmitter/receiver demonstrate no destructive effects and low SEU and SEFI cross-sections. In addition the 050-301 devices demonstrate no sensitivity to neutron irradiation after a fluence of 2.5E+12n/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and only a small increase in supply current, but no change in functionality after (Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>) TID exposures up to 250 krad(Si). The Glenair 050-346, also known as “parallel optics”, 40 Gbps (4 channels x10 Gbps each) transceiver was also tested with heavy ions and exhibited no destructive effects and very low SEFI and SEU sensitivity.

articleTitle: Neutron Induced Single Event Upset (SEU) Testing of Commercial Flash Memory Devices with and without Embedded Error Correction Codes (ECC)
abstract: Results of neutron induced single event upset testing of the Spansion (Cypress) 128Mb, 90nm, S29GL128P and 256Mb, 65nm, S25FL256S MirrorBit NOR Flash memory, the latter with embedded error correction codes, are described.Five samples of each memory type were irradiated with a 14-MeV neutron source. The units were tested after irradiated statically as well as under bias using different combinations of continual read/write/erase/correct loops and using a variety of bit patterns. Results for Single Event Latchup (SEL), Single Event Functional Interrupt (SEFI) and correctable and uncorrectable Single Event Upset (SEU) errors are presented along with cross section data and soft error rates.

articleTitle: A Summary of MIL STD 750, Method 1017 Neutron Irradiation Tests Performed on JANSR2N3700, JANSR2N2369; JANSR2N2222; and JANSR2N2907 Bipolar Junction Transistors (July 2019)
abstract: This work will show the results of neutron interactions on 4 JANSR (100kRad) bipolar junction transistors (BJTs). The tests were carried out as per MIL STD 750, Method 1017. The total integral neutron fluence was stepped at 5 levels between 5. $0\mathrm{x}10^{11}\mathrm{n}/\mathrm{c}\mathrm{m}^{2}$ and $1.0\mathrm{x}10^{14} \mathrm{n}/\mathrm{c}\mathrm{m}^{2}$. The effects of this neutron bombardment are consistent with those of displacement damage. The primary effects were $\mathrm{h}_{F\mathrm{E}}$ degredation combined with increasing ICES and ICBO over increasing fluence. Secondary effects include a rise in VCESAT and a slight rise in BVCEO. While not specifically tested, it is believed that dynamic parameters are impacted by $\mathrm{h}_{F\mathrm{E}}$ reduction including the storage time in the BE junction in switching applications and BVcBo/BVcEO approaching unity. The end goal of this work is to offer an explanation of neutron irradiation that is useful in a switching power circuit design

articleTitle: Impact of Single Event Effects on Key Electronic Components for COTS-based Satellite Systems
abstract: Single Event Effect (SEE) testing of key electronic components for Commercial off-the-Shelf (COTS)-based space systems is undertaken to understand their SEE sensitivity. Results show how the SEE manifestations, which are capable of interrupting normal operation of the electronics, can be tolerable with simple mitigation techniques while deployed in orbit.
